topic.title: Passing Objects to Methods
topic.description: How objects are passed to methods

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how objects travel between methods in Java? Let's break it down!

• How Java passes objects to methods (it's not what you think!)
• The difference between passing objects vs. primitive types
• How to modify objects inside methods safely

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a library. You don't carry the actual book around - you just show your library card (reference) to access it. That's exactly how Java passes objects!

When you pass an object to a method:
• You're actually passing a *reference* (like a library card) to the object
• The method can use this reference to interact with the original object
• Changes made inside the method affect the original object

This is different from primitive types (like `int` or `double`), which are passed by *value* - like making a photocopy of a page instead of showing your library card.

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Passing Objects to Methods works:

steps.title: Object Creation
steps.description: First, we create an object in memory. Think of it like writing a book and placing it on a shelf.

steps.title: Method Call
steps.description: When we pass the object to a method, we're actually passing its memory address (reference). The method gets a 'library card' to the original object.

steps.title: Method Execution
steps.description: The method uses the reference to modify the original object. The changes persist after the method ends!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Objects are passed by *reference* (like a library card)
✓ Primitives are passed by *value* (like a photocopy)
✓ Changes to objects inside methods affect the original
✓ The method can call the object's methods using the reference
✓ Passing objects is memory-efficient (no copies made)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use clear parameter names to show you're working with objects
Document if your method modifies the passed object
Consider making objects immutable if they shouldn't change
donts: Don't assume primitives and objects behave the same way
Don't modify objects unexpectedly (it can cause bugs)
Don't forget that `null` can be passed as an object reference
sections.protip: Use `final` for method parameters if you want to prevent reassigning the reference (though the object itself can still be modified!)

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Passing Objects to Methods used in real apps?

examples.how: When you transfer money, the `Account` objects are passed to transaction methods that modify their balances
Player objects are passed to collision detection methods that update their positions and health
User objects are passed to methods that update profiles, add friends, or post content

problem.description: Create a `Rectangle` class with width and height fields. Write a method that takes a Rectangle object and doubles its size. Then create a test program that shows the rectangle's dimensions before and after the method call.
hints: Remember: the method should modify the original object
You'll need to use the setters to change the dimensions
The method should take a Rectangle parameter
problem.explanation: The method receives a reference to the original Rectangle object. By calling its setters, we modify the original object's fields. The changes persist after the method ends because we worked with the actual object, not a copy.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Objects are passed by reference - methods work with the original object
📌 Primitives are passed by value - methods get a copy
📌 Practice creating and modifying objects through methods
📌 You're ready to learn about returning objects from methods next!
